key_facts: **Angiokeratomas**: dark red to black papules from dilated superficial capillaries with overlying hyperkeratosis.
Variants: solitary (legs; can mimic melanoma), **Fordyce** (scrotum/vulva), Mibelli (fingers/toes), circumscriptum (congenital).
**Multiple angiokeratomas in a bathing-trunk area** suggest **Fabry disease** (X-linked α-galactosidase A deficiency).
Fabry clues: neuropathic pain in hands and feet, reduced sweating, proteinuria, early stroke or cardiac disease.
Refer uncertain dark lesions; refer suspected Fabry for testing at a national lysosomal storage centre.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: Benign vascular lesions: dilated superficial dermal capillaries with overlying hyperkeratosis.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Ectatic papillary dermal vessels with reactive epidermal thickening. **Angiokeratoma corporis diffusum** (multiple lesions) is a marker of lysosomal storage disease. The classic one is **Fabry disease**: X-linked, **GLA** gene, α-galactosidase A deficiency, with globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulating in vessels, kidney, heart and nerves. Others are fucosidosis and sialidosis.

ul: **"A black papule that bleeds must be melanoma"**: angiokeratoma is a common mimic; dermoscopy helps, but refer if uncertain.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Angiokeratomas are **ectatic papillary vessels** with a thickened epidermis on top.

mech.t: Superficial dermal capillaries dilate (pressure, trauma or storage material).
The overlying epidermis thickens and becomes hyperkeratotic.
mech.caption: Angiokeratoma: dilated vessels hugged by a thickened epidermis.

mech.t: Gb3 accumulates in vessel walls, kidney, heart and nerves.

blocks: Fabry features: acroparaesthesia (burning hands/feet triggered by heat, exercise, fever) starting in childhood; **hypohidrosis** and heat intolerance; cornea verticillata; proteinuria and later renal failure; left ventricular hypertrophy and arrhythmias; stroke at a young age. Heterozygous women are often affected too.

ul: Dermoscopy: red-blue lacunae, whitish veil, and haemorrhagic crusts.
Biopsy if a dark lesion could be melanoma.
**Fabry:** α-Gal A enzyme activity in males; GLA gene testing (needed in females); plasma lyso-Gb3. Urine protein, eGFR, ECG/echo.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: Melanoma or pigmented BCC (dark solitary lesion), cherry angioma, haemangioma, venous lake, Kaposi sarcoma, warts (on the hands), pyogenic granuloma, and lymphangioma circumscriptum.

ul: Benign isolated angiokeratomas: reassure. Treatment is cosmetic (laser, cautery, excision; specialist/not NHS-funded).
**Uncertain dark lesion → refer** (dermoscopy/biopsy). Use NG12 urgency if the 7-point score is ≥3.

**Multiple angiokeratomas in a bathing-trunk distribution, or with neuropathic pain, sweating problems, proteinuria or early cardiac/stroke history → refer** to dermatology/GP for **Fabry testing**. Diagnosis and treatment are at a **national lysosomal storage disorder centre** (enzyme replacement with agalsidase alfa/beta, pegunigalsidase alfa; or oral migalastat for amenable mutations). Cascade-screen family members.
Neuropathic pain in Fabry: specialist-guided (carbamazepine, gabapentinoids). Avoid triggers.

ladder.t: Reassure isolated angiokeratomas; treatment is cosmetic (laser, cautery, excision; not NHS-funded).
Uncertain dark lesion → refer (dermoscopy / biopsy); NG12 urgency if 7-point ≥ 3.

Bathing-trunk angiokeratomas, neuropathic pain, sweating problems, proteinuria or early cardiac / stroke history → **Fabry testing**. National lysosomal storage centre: enzyme replacement (agalsidase alfa / beta, pegunigalsidase alfa) or oral **migalastat** (amenable mutations); cascade-screen family.

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Migalastat**: Every other day; no food 2 h before and after.

refer.t: Many angiokeratomas in a child / young adult with burning hand / foot pain, reduced sweating or proteinuria: test for **Fabry**.
Solitary changing dark papule you can’t confidently call an angiokeratoma: **possible melanoma**.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Many angiokeratomas in a child or young adult with burning hand/foot pain, reduced sweating or proteinuria: test for **Fabry disease**.
Solitary changing dark papule: if you cannot confidently call it an angiokeratoma, refer as a **possible melanoma**.
Bleeding; in Fabry, renal failure, cardiomyopathy and stroke.

pearls: Fordyce angiokeratomas bleeding on the scrotum are benign, but **always ask about other symptoms** (the patient is often embarrassed).
